correctness.rationale: Analytic derivation verifies event probability, conditional merger-history law, normalized exponential waiting times, exact rational-harmonic conditional mean and covariance, sign, and coupling to ordinary (n−1)-sample external length. The nonnegative discrepancy has mean 4(H_n−3/2)/(n−2)→0 and the ordinary external-length variance is O(log n/n). Independent exhaustive exact-history enumeration through seven leaves and exact arithmetic through n=500 corroborate all finite identities, but are not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new conditional aggregate law is distinguished from the inspected unconditioned external-branch length theorems, individual branch-start/end distributions, and cherry-count covariances. Public 2020 root-balance literature is closely adjacent but its abstract specifically studies the longest individual edge rather than the sum conditioned on a singleton basal split. Its inaccessible full text is an explicit residual historical-priority risk, not a demonstrated covering theorem.
residual_risks: Full text of Disanto–Wiehe 2020, with its focus on longest external edges and root balance, was not accessible and could conceivably contain an equivalent total-length conditional result.
The 2021 compendium and certain earlier single-branch references were not reviewed in complete full text.
Searches and limited access cannot establish absolute historical priority or independence of validation.

value.rationale: The (1,n−1) basal split is a maximally unbalanced genealogical topology with exact rarity 2/(n−1). Despite unconditional total-external-length concentration at two, conditioning produces a nondegenerate excess equal to coalescent height plus two. This identifies a natural rare topological cause of order-one excess external mutation opportunity and quantifies finite-sample association by an exact positive covariance. It addresses an interpretable conditioning gap rather than a cosmetic reparameterization.
